title: Strings & bytes
description: NUL-terminated C strings vs explicit length
theory:
### Bytes, not abstract text

In this track, strings are **byte sequences** with a known length. UTF-8 literals in
the assembler appear exactly as the bytes you wrote between quotes; NASM does not interpret
them as Unicode code points beyond encoding those bytes.

For truly dynamic text you either format into a scratch buffer or emit digits by repeated
division—classic **itoa**-style loops—or use libc helpers when you link with **gcc**.

### `write`-friendly layouts

Place literals in **`.data`** (`db 'H', 'e', 'l', 'l', 'o'`) and compute **`len equ $ - msg`**
so lengths stay consistent when you edit content. When printing single computed digits,
materialize ASCII by adding **`'0'`** into a byte buffer in **`.bss`**.

```nasm
section .data
    greeting: db 'Hello', 10
    glen equ $ - greeting

section .text
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, greeting
    mov rdx, glen
    syscall
```

### NUL terminators are optional

C strings end at **`0`**, but **syscalls** consume explicit lengths. Do not assume a
NUL unless you call routines that do; mixing models is a common off-by-one source.

exercises.title: Quoted word
exercises.description: Print exactly `go` (two letters, no newline) from a `.data` label, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    w: db 'g','o'
    wlen equ $ - w
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    w: db 'g', 'o'
    wlen equ $ - w
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel w]
    mov rdx, wlen
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Two writes
exercises.description: Print `ab` by issuing **two** `write` syscalls (first prints `a`, second prints `b`), no newline, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    a: db 'a'
    b: db 'b'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    a: db 'a'
    b: db 'b'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel a]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel b]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: NUL-terminated but not printed
exercises.description: Define `db 'Z',0` in `.data`. Print only the `Z` (length **1**, not including the NUL), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    z: db 'Z', 0
section .text
_start:
    ; write 1 byte from address z
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: The NUL exists for interoperability; `rdx` must still be `1` here
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    z: db 'Z', 0
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel z]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Counted string length
exercises.description: Define `db 'h','i',0` in `.data`. Use **`len equ $ - msg - 1`** style: put the bytes under label `msg` including the trailing `0`, then compute the length **excluding** the NUL (`$ - msg - 1`). Print exactly `hi` with one `write`, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'h','i',0
    ; len equ $ - msg - 1
section .text
_start:
    ; write stdout, rsi=msg, rdx=len
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `len equ $ - msg - 1` subtracts the terminating `0` byte
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'h', 'i', 0
    len equ $ - msg - 1
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel msg]
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
